questions.q: What does GROUP BY TICKET_DATE, PRIORITY accomplish in the summary query?
options: Sorts the rows by date and priority without changing the row count
Filters out rows that don't have a priority set
Removes duplicate tickets regardless of date or priority
Collapses rows into one summary row per day-and-priority combination, matching the grain decided in Lesson 1
questions.explain: GROUP BY produces one row per unique combination of the grouping columns — here, one row per day and priority, which is the project's defined grain.

questions.q: Why does the query filter the current month in the WHERE clause rather than with a HAVING clause after grouping?
options: WHERE clauses are not allowed before GROUP BY in Snowflake
WHERE filters raw rows before grouping, which is both correct and cheaper since Snowflake never touches last month's rows at all
HAVING and WHERE behave identically in Snowflake, so it doesn't matter
HAVING can only be used with COUNT(*), never with date filters
questions.explain: HAVING filters groups after they're formed; filtering rows out before grouping with WHERE is both the correct approach and more efficient.

questions.q: What does DATE_TRUNC('DAY', CREATED_AT)::DATE do in this query?
options: Deletes the time portion from the underlying raw table
Converts the column to a string for display
Collapses each ticket's exact timestamp down to its calendar day and casts it to a plain date
Rounds the timestamp up to the next day
questions.explain: DATE_TRUNC rounds down to the start of the day, and ::DATE casts the result from a timestamp to a plain date, matching what the VP actually needs to see.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the sanity-check query that sums TICKET_COUNT by priority?
options: To replace the main summary query entirely
To load additional ticket data into the raw table
To grant the analyst role access to the view
To confirm the daily summary query's math is internally consistent before presenting it to the stakeholder
questions.explain: Rolling daily counts back up to one total per priority is a quick way to catch an obviously wrong query before anyone relies on the numbers.

questions.q: What is COUNT(*) measuring in this query?
options: The number of support tickets in each day-and-priority group
The number of days in the current month
The total number of priority levels that exist
The number of distinct columns in RAW_TICKETS
questions.explain: COUNT(*) is the actual metric the VP asked for — how many tickets fall into each day-and-priority combination.
